_about: PARKED. The traded-blows set piece and the two charges at range, with the meeting in the middle. Not loaded, not hashed. Times in ticks. Rules quoted are Game Design's (docs/design/agency-pass.md sections 1 and 2); the staging follows Legal's twelve rules (docs/legal/agency-pass-screen.md). Our own staging throughout.

blowForBlow.label: Blow for Blow: an in-house label only, never a title, tag or logo; Narrative picks the player-facing name

rules.trigger: both fighters release a power blow on the flash in the same exchange
rules.turn: a heavy press on the beat, inside an 8-tick window
rules.blow: x0.7 of a heavy; the other takes it and stays up; then it is his turn
rules.afterMax: both slide apart with no winner: the double slide
rules.end: the first to miss the beat, or to guard or dodge, gives way; the other lands the last blow as an earned launch, with the panel and 25% more impact wear
rules.brink: a blow that breaks a region ends it
rules.budget: one big set piece per 20 s

locationRule: each turn uses a different strike and a different location from the turn before
no fighter repeats a strike in one set piece
never two hand blows to the ribs or flank running: limb families alternate
the wear goes to the location's region, not always to the core (a change to Game Design's 'to the core')

travel.what: they never stand still: each blow drives both along the ground. The taker gives the distance on his feet, the striker follows through it, and the answer drives them back the other way, further each time
travel.ground: the pair ploughs one lengthening furrow, there and back; World cuts it by tier
travel.air: the same drive through the air, with a ring leaving each blow

turnBeats: 0: the striker's blow lands, on the beat
0 to 10: both travel the turn's drive; the taker is in his brace, on his feet
by 14: the taker is set again and the roles swap
the last 10 ticks of the beat: the wind-up of his answer
the next beat: his answer lands

poses.look: His own brace: both forearm plates drawn tight against his ribs, the lead shoulder rolled forward and the chin behind it, the spine upright. He gives ground on his heels and does not fold.
poses.limits: elbows bent inside 160 degrees; the rear thigh at most 45 degrees behind the hip; no arm straight back

poses.look: A heavy hook dug in along the ribs: the elbow at a right angle, the hip turned through, the other forearm plate across his own chest.
poses.limits: the upper arm's twist inside 100 degrees with the elbow bent

poses.look: A straight heavy blow to the chest from a low shoulder: arm, spine and rear leg one line.
poses.limits: the elbow short of 160 degrees; the rear thigh at most 45 back

reused: the slide on the feet (the taker's travel)
the over-commit, for a blow that missed its beat
the computed reaction at low strength over the brace
the wear layers, for the one who gives way
wave 1's heavies, aimed at the turn's location
camera: the director's wide shot: both bodies, their feet and the furrow in frame
it tracks the pair as they travel; it does not cut back and forth between them
one push-in after the third blow and one after the sixth, no more
no freeze on a hit and no close-up of a straining face
on the last blow it widens along the launch
legal: it starts from the exchange: nobody lowers a guard or invites a blow
each fighter takes it in his own brace; the On the Chin stance is not used here
a different strike and location each turn
no fixed alternating camera and no freeze
at most one short line per fighter, from his own bank
the world answers by biome: a crack or a furrow, no rising ring of rubble, no lightning
the one who gives way shows his own wear stage and reaction
no folding over, clutching or gasping

ranged._source: Game Design, agency-pass.md section 1 (Orb's pick). A strike never exists at range

bands.mid: 3 to 12 bh: a short lunge of 20 ticks at most, then the wind-up; the stick picks the entry
bands.far: beyond 12 bh: tap to taunt, hold to charge

farTaunt._note: his taunt gestures at three quarters of their close length, played while he keeps flying; no beckoning

rules.feint: releasing the button stops the charge at no cost
rules.blasts: any blast that lands stops him
rules.arrival: a light opener, into a brawl

lightCharge.gather: 12 ticks: he drops a shoulder toward the rival; derives from the dash's launch-off

feintPiece.look: The stop of a feint: he turns side-on to the line and brakes, the leading arm swung wide, one knee up.
feintPiece.limits: the raised thigh inside the hip's 170 degrees forward

rules.committed: only a dodge-cancel (15 ki) stops it
rules.blasts: light blasts and volleys do half damage and do not stop him; a charged shot or a beam does
rules.arrival: a charged heavy; landing clean, it earns a launch

heavyCharge.gather: 24 ticks: the charge pose, the forearm plates lighting

flightPose.look: Both forearm plates side by side ahead of him, never crossed, head tucked behind them, the body one low line.
flightPose.limits: both shoulders inside their cone with the elbows bent; no arm straight back

heavyCharge.shrug: the computed reaction at low strength over the flight pose

meeting.rule: the far taunt answered by an attack press: both rush and meet in the middle; a fist clash if either pressed heavy, otherwise a blur exchange, on the pulse
meeting.how: each covers half the distance on a straight dash and they arrive on the same tick, at the midpoint, at contact distance
camera: from the taunt's face cut-in to a wide shot that holds both
it tightens evenly as they close, with the meeting at the centre of the frame

ranged.legal: the charges follow the dash rule: not both arms trailed straight back, not one fist punched ahead, and he is drawn the whole way with no vanish
